findings.claim: Growth comes in jumps: the four biggest videos carry 66.1% of all lifetime net subscribers, three of them Chhava-window Shorts.
findings.note: Measured 2026-09-28 at 69.8% on the full daily series from each video's publish date. The 100k plan is sized on breakouts because of this.

findings.claim: The same script's Instagram and YouTube results are unrelated: r = 0.07 across matched reels, so a result on one platform is no evidence for the other.
findings.note: 2026-09-21: r = -0.10 on 36 pairs. Basis of the platform-segregation rule.

findings.claim: Card count is a production lever: 9-10 card carousels reach 25.7x what single images do on the median.
findings.note: 2026-09-21: median reach 281 at one card, 13.6k at 9-10.

findings.claim: Instagram carousels reach about 4 times what reels do on the median (3.77x).
findings.note: Supersedes the withdrawn 35x claim, which came from the 90-day window.

findings.claim: Reach is not conversion on Instagram: among feed posts over 20,000 reach, follows per 1,000 reach spans 653x from worst to best.
Instagram has more followers than the YouTube channel has subscribers (gap: 7,731).
Reels under 45 percent skip break 20,000 reach 12x as often as reels above it.
findings.note: 2026-09-21: 20% vs 2%, about 10x. A null value means no reel above 45 percent ever broke out, which still supports the gate.

findings.claim: Before August 2026 every long-form view was also an engaged view: engaged views were 100.0% of views from January 2025 to July 2026.
findings.note: Measured 2026-11-14: 100.0 in every month. The baseline that makes the August break visible.

findings.claim: From August 2026 long-form views overstate real viewing: engaged views are only 41.8% of views, so long-form view counts before and after August 2026 are not comparable. Compare engaged views across that line.
findings.note: Measured 2026-11-14: 62% Aug, 40% Sep, 32% Oct 2026. Old videos fell too (62% on views since August), so it is a counting change, not weaker videos. Drift (back above 80) means YouTube changed the counting again.

findings.claim: The long-form gap sits in the Home feed (reported as SUBSCRIBER): only 36.1% of Home-feed long-form views since August 2026 are engaged views, while suggested, external and notification views stay near 100 percent.
findings.note: Measured 2026-11-14: SUBSCRIBER 36%, YT_SEARCH 42%, RELATED_VIDEO 97%, EXT_URL 100%. Both low surfaces autoplay previews; that cause is inferred, not documented by YouTube.

findings.claim: Over the last 28 days long-form still earns most upload-attributed net subscribers (now 70.9%).
Long-form earns about 80 percent of the subscribers uploads bring in (now 80.7%), while being under a fifth of the output.
findings.note: CLAUDE.md 2026-09-21: long-form 17% of output, 80% of subscribers. own_video_lifetime, gross subs.

findings.claim: One long-form view is worth many Shorts views in subscribers: long-form converts 8.63x as well per view.
Long-form carries about three quarters of upload watch time (now 74.7%).
Community posts buy views, not subscribers: 0.007 subscribers per 1,000 post views.
Over the channel's whole life Shorts earned 70.9% of net subscribers. Long-form's 80% share is a 365-day reading (long_subs_share_365d); always quote that finding with its window.
findings.note: Measured 2026-09-28 at 72.5% (8,020 of 11,066). Old viral Shorts (Sambhaji, Tarabai, Turban) fall outside the 365-day window.

findings.claim: Most channel-wide subscriber growth is not attributable to any upload: uploads account for 49.1% of net subscribers (viral community post, homepage subscriptions).
findings.note: 2026-09-27: 117 of 830. Will drift once the community post stops sending subscribers; that is the signal to re-base growth.ts.

findings.claim: WhatsApp sends YouTube 28x as many views as Instagram does; Instagram is a parallel audience, not a feeder.
findings.note: 12,013 vs 378 on 2026-09-21. Referrer names are merged the same way as normaliseReferrer() in distribution.ts.

findings.claim: Chakla alone is about 42 percent of all long-form views in the year (now 21.0%); the library's reach is one video.
findings.note: Video id novRBQc_w2c. Expected to fall as it has stopped earning; drift here is good news if other long-form is rising.

findings.claim: No reel that passed 20,000 reach had a skip rate above the reel median (worst breakout minus median: 25.8 points).
findings.note: Basis of the 45 percent skip gate. 2026-09-21: worst breakout 47.2 against a 54.6 median.

findings.claim: Long-form converts at roughly 15 subscribers per 1,000 views (now 8.5).
Search, not the Shorts feed, is where Shorts views come from: 26.8% of Shorts views arrive from YouTube search.
The channel grows at about 9 net subscribers a day and reaches 100,000 in 2038.
findings.note: Withdrawn 2026-09-27. That was the upload-attributed rate; channel-wide (channel_totals_daily) it was about 30 to 39 a day. Quote channel_wide.subs_per_day_28d instead.

findings.claim: Instagram carousels get 35x the reach of reels.
findings.note: Withdrawn 2026-09-21. From the 90-day window, which happened to be strong for carousels and weak for reels. All-time median ratio is about 4x.

findings.claim: Instagram is a feeder that sends its audience to YouTube.
findings.note: Withdrawn 2026-09-21. Instagram referred about 378 YouTube views in a year against WhatsApp's 12,013.

findings.claim: The Punjabi-Mexican reel flopped because its 65.6 percent skip rate was above typical.
findings.note: Withdrawn 2026-09-21. A sample of one against an unmeasured baseline; the reel median skip rate is about the same.

findings.claim: YouTube Shorts pay 4.4x for the freedom lane, so Shorts should stay in the freedom lane and carousel topics should not go to YouTube.
findings.note: Withdrawn 2026-09-21. Computed from own_video_metrics, a 90-day window that contained the 18 August Netaji anniversary. On own_video_lifetime (365 days) the revision and freedom lanes are level on Shorts, and revision wins everywhere else it is measurable.
